title: ProphetRouterRL: A Reinforcement Learning Enhanced Routing Protocol for V2X Delay Tolerant Networks
content: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks may experience intermittent connectivity and frequent link disruption due to high node mobility, variable density, and heterogeneous mobility patterns. When a contemporaneous end-to-end path cannot be guaranteed, Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) enables message delivery through store-carry-forward communication. Among DTN routing protocols, PRoPHET exploits historical and transitive encounters to estimate destination-specific delivery predictability. However, its conventional Greater Than (GRTR) forwarding rule has limited contextual awareness because relay selection is based primarily on relative delivery predictability. This paper proposes ProphetRouterRL, a two-stage routing protocol that augments PRoPHET with Q-learning. First, PRoPHET identifies eligible relay candidates satisfying ΔP > 0. A Q-learning agent then determines whether to send or hold each message using a six-dimensional state comprising relay-buffer availability, encounter history, message load, remaining time-to-live, hop count, and node type. ProphetRouterRL was evaluated against conventional PRoPHET using the ONE Simulator in a map-based urban scenario representing the UKM Bangi area in Malaysia. The seven-day simulation comprised 129 heterogeneous nodes, including pedestrians, cyclists, cars, buses, metro trains, and stationary communication points. ProphetRouterRL increased the delivery probability from 46.47% to 93.12%, while reducing routing overhead and average latency by 39.4% and 41.4%, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of combining PRoPHET’s delivery-predictability estimation with context-aware learned forwarding decisions in opportunistic V2X environments.
